objective: Measure fixed-context backbone scaling through the existing execution path on the Q3_K 780M model.

findings: All 12 fixed-context runs used Vulkan0 and passed finite output, expected hidden/logit shapes, final state position, and exact repeated hidden/logit equality checks.
Mean final n=1 host time rises from approximately 12.76 ms at context 64 to 28.05 ms at context 1024; this is a backbone diagnostic on synthetic prefixes, not speech RTF.
The fixed-context process order was varied across three rounds (ascending, descending, rotated) and per-process samples are retained for variation analysis.

Logger shape keys identify prefill QK and V*P as the f32 m/n/k attention matmuls and final n=1 QK/V*P as the corresponding MUL_MAT_VEC shapes; profile totals are perturbed attribution and are not end-to-end timing claims.
Prefill profiling at context 1024 shows large q4_K FFN matmuls and growing attention QK/V*P work; no custom attention or runtime changes were made.
limitations: The model is Q3_K and inputs are deterministic synthetic initialized prefixes.
No speech quality, Mandarin quality, audio, or RTF conclusion is supported by this artifact.
Logger runs alter scheduling and timing; use fixed-context host timing for scaling and logger blocks only for operation attribution.
The pod was released after all timing/logger processes exited; no extra GPU experiment was run.
Core/shared-library SHA256 values were collected after measurement; no before/after pair was retained.
